input: The uptake of a dye from water by a metal-organic framework was examined in batch tests at 298 K, and the results can be summarised as follows. The fitted Langmuir capacity was 193 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 5, indicating the level of uptake that the fitted isotherm approaches at its plateau. With an adsorbent dose of 0.7 g L-1, the removal after 120 min reached 85% of the initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1, showing that a substantial proportion of the dye was taken up within the duration of the test. Batch tests bring a fixed mass of adsorbent into contact with the dye solution in a closed vessel, and the removal is read from the change in the liquid concentration over the contact time. A qualification should nevertheless be attached to the capacity figure: the Langmuir fit is reported for pH 5 only, and capacity at other pH values was not measured, so the result belongs to the conditions studied and should not be assumed to hold more generally. The two headline figures therefore complement one another, the capacity describing the material's fitted ceiling and the removal describing what was actually achieved in the test as run.
target: Adsorption of a dye from water on a metal-organic framework reached 85% removal of the initial dye concentration after 120 min in batch tests at 298 K, at an adsorbent dose of 0.7 g L-1 and an initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1. The fitted Langmuir capacity was 193 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 5. Batch tests bring a fixed mass of adsorbent into contact with the dye solution in a closed vessel, and the removal is read from the fall in the liquid concentration over the contact time. The capacity is a fitted plateau value from the isotherm fitted to the batch data, and the fit is reported for pH 5 only. Capacity at other pH values was not measured, so no capacity figure exists for any other condition of acidity. Removal and capacity answer different questions: the removal states what the tested dose achieved against the stated starting concentration in the stated time, and the capacity states the fitted ceiling on uptake per gram of adsorbent. The two figures are reported together because a capacity without the achieved removal, or a removal without the fitted capacity, would each describe only part of the test outcome. Both stand on the same batch tests, at the stated temperature. A comparison against another adsorbent is supported only at the tested pH and under the tested conditions; beyond them, the pair of figures does not travel.
